name: public-primary-reference-holdout-24
notes: Verified subset of generated candidate cohort H01-H24 (ids retained). Same format as cohort.json.
References ground human expected labels only. References and rationales MUST NOT be passed to models.
Not blind; do not tune prompts on this split.
Top-up round 1: T104 and T112-T125 appended (ids retained from the top-up candidates T101-T125).

cases.text: The 2022 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Qatar.
cases.rationale: FIFA's tournament page lists Qatar as host of the 2022 men's World Cup.

cases.text: The 2022 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Saudi Arabia.
cases.rationale: FIFA lists Qatar, not Saudi Arabia, as host of the 2022 tournament.

cases.text: The EU General Data Protection Regulation has applied since 25 May 2018.
cases.rationale: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 was adopted in 2016 and, by its final provisions, applies from 25 May 2018.

cases.text: The EU General Data Protection Regulation has applied since 2012.
cases.rationale: The regulation was proposed in 2012 but adopted in 2016 and applies from 2018.

cases.text: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.
cases.rationale: The Louvre collection record attributes the portrait to Leonardo da Vinci.

cases.text: The Mona Lisa was painted by Michelangelo.
cases.rationale: The Louvre attributes the work to Leonardo, not Michelangelo.

cases.text: The Riemann hypothesis is true.
cases.rationale: The Clay Mathematics Institute lists it as an unsolved Millennium Prize problem; it is neither proved nor disproved.

cases.text: P does not equal NP.
cases.rationale: The Clay Mathematics Institute lists P versus NP as an open Millennium Prize problem; no accepted proof either way.

cases.text: The Voynich manuscript contains a message in a natural language.
cases.rationale: Yale's Beinecke Library describes the manuscript's script as undeciphered; its nature remains unresolved, not shown to be a hoax or a language.

cases.text: Electric cars produce no emissions.
cases.rationale: The US Department of Energy says all-electric operation has zero tailpipe emissions but upstream power-generation emissions still count. The statement omits the tailpipe versus life-cycle distinction; a life-cycle reading can reasonably be judged false.
cases.scoringNote: Context-sensitive gold. Report strict four-label score and a sensitivity score accepting alternativeExpected; also report the non-context-sensitive cases separately. Do not tune on these examples.

cases.text: Sweden has been a NATO member since 2023.
cases.rationale: NATO states Sweden deposited its accession instrument on 7 March 2024, becoming the 32nd member, so 2023 is the common but wrong year.

cases.text: NATO has 31 member countries.
cases.rationale: NATO's page lists 32 member countries after Sweden joined in 2024; 31 was the count from Finland's 2023 accession until then.

cases.text: The euro is the currency of 20 European Union member states.
cases.rationale: The ECB page lists euro banknotes as legal tender in 21 of 27 member states, with Bulgaria joining in 2026; 20 is the pre-2026 count that older search results still show.

cases.text: China is the most populous country in the world.
cases.rationale: The UN page describes China as having the second-largest population, with India now the most populous; many older pages still say China.

cases.text: The US Supreme Court overruled Chevron deference in Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo.
cases.rationale: The Court held in June 2024 that courts must use independent judgment on statutory meaning rather than defer to ambiguous agency readings, overruling Chevron.

cases.text: The International Space Station has been continuously occupied since November 2000.
cases.rationale: NASA marked 25 years of continuous human presence aboard the ISS on 2 November 2025.

cases.text: The IARC classifies drinking coffee as possibly carcinogenic to humans.
cases.rationale: IARC reclassified coffee drinking in 2016 as Group 3, not classifiable, reversing its earlier 2B listing, though very hot beverages were rated probably carcinogenic. Older results still cite 2B.

cases.text: Google Chrome has phased out third-party cookies for all users.
cases.rationale: Google said in April 2025 that it would keep its current approach, with no standalone prompt, and users keep choosing cookie settings in Chrome; the planned full phase-out did not happen.

cases.text: Windows 10 reached its end of support date on 14 October 2025.
cases.rationale: Microsoft's support page states Windows 10 support ended on 14 October 2025 for standard updates.

cases.text: Smallpox is the only infectious disease that WHO has declared eradicated in humans.
cases.rationale: WHO says smallpox is the only infectious disease to achieve this distinction, declared in 1980.

cases.text: Pele is the only footballer to have won three men's World Cups.
cases.rationale: FIFA's tribute states Pele is the only player to win three World Cups, in 1958, 1962 and 1970.

cases.text: The Gotthard Base Tunnel in Switzerland is the world's longest railway tunnel.
cases.rationale: UIC reports the 57 km Gotthard Base Tunnel, inaugurated in June 2016, is the world's longest and deepest railway tunnel, surpassing Japan's Seikan.

cases.text: Bob Dylan won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016.
cases.rationale: The Nobel Prize site lists Dylan as the 2016 literature laureate for new poetic expressions within the American song tradition; the choice was controversial, not disputed as fact.

cases.text: The US dollar accounts for less than half of global foreign exchange reserves.
cases.rationale: IMF COFER data put the dollar share near 57 percent in late 2025, a century low but still well above half; headlines about decline can mislead.
